{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Michael S. Jacobson''' is a mathematician, and Professor of Mathematical & Statistical Sciences in the Department of Mathematical & Statistical Science at the [[University of Colorado Denver]].  He served as Chair from 2003 to 2012 and was on loan serving as a program director in EHR/DUE at the [[National Science Foundation]].

==Early life==
Jacobson did his undergraduate studies at [[SUNY Stony Brook]] in mathematics, graduating in 1975 and received his MS and Ph.D. in 1977 and 1980, respectively, from [[Emory University]] under the supervision of [[Henry S. Sharp Jr.]]<ref>{{cite web|title=The Mathematics Genealogy Project|url=http://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=2257|accessdate=21 July 2011}}</ref> He spent 23 years at the [[University of Louisville]], where in addition to being promoted to Professor in 1988, also served as Department Chair and Associate Dean for Research and Graduate Studies.<ref>{{cite web|last=Jacobson|first=Michael|title=Curriculum Vitae|url=http://math.ucdenver.edu/~msj/UCD-vita.pdf|accessdate=21 July 2011}}</ref>

==Current work==
Jacobson has been at the University of Colorado Denver since 2003.

==Mathematics==
Jacobson specializes in [[combinatorics]] and in particular [[graph theory]]. He has published more than 140 mathematical papers on topics including [[Ramsey theory]], [[Hamiltonian graph]]s, [[dominating set|domination in graphs]] and [[extremal graph theory]].  He has had over 70 collaborators including [[Kenneth Bogart]], [[Stefan Burr]], [[Gary Chartrand]], [[Guantao Chen]], [[Paul Erdős]], [[Ralph Faudree]], [[Ronald Gould (mathematician)|Ron Gould]], [[András Gyárfás]], [[Frank Harary]], [[Stephen Hedetniemi]], [[Linda Lesniak]], [[Fred McMorris]], [[K. Brooks Reid]], [[Richard Schelp]], [[Edward Scheinerman]] and [[Douglas B. West]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Jacobson|first=Michael|title=Publications List|url=http://math.ucdenver.edu/~msj/PublicationList.pdf|accessdate=21 July 2011}}</ref>
